biography.plain_text: David Serls was an American metals businessman who owned Colonial Metals in Columbia, Pennsylvania. The company recycled scrap into brass, bronze and copper ingots for foundries. He served as its chairman and chief operating officer, combining ownership with industrial management, and made his home in Sewalls Point on Florida's Atlantic coast.

long_biography.plain_text:
As president of the Institute of Scrap Recycling Industries, David Serls helped broaden an industry rooted in metal recovery. At its first plastics seminar and roundtable in 1990, he announced plans to give plastics recycling a permanent committee. The board established the committee the following month, with a mandate to organise another industry meeting and develop specifications for plastic scrap. The association's next specifications circular included definitions for twenty-seven types of plastic scrap.

Away from business, Serls collected antique cars, rode motorcycles and enjoyed gardening. He also followed the Baltimore Orioles and Ravens and the Philadelphia Flyers.
long_biography.html:
As president of the Institute of Scrap Recycling Industries, David Serls helped broaden an industry rooted in metal recovery. At its first plastics seminar and roundtable in 1990, he announced plans to give plastics recycling a permanent committee. The board established the committee the following month, with a mandate to organise another industry meeting and develop specifications for plastic scrap. The association's next specifications circular included definitions for twenty-seven types of plastic scrap.

Away from business, Serls collected antique cars, rode motorcycles and enjoyed gardening. He also followed the Baltimore Orioles and Ravens and the Philadelphia Flyers.
